Trains do not have differentials. This gif explain how they turn.

Let's say it a single car. At some point (x ) number of wheels is off the ground. It's heavy and fast and smilingly complicated/difficult to drive operate properly. And that information has some terrifing qualities to it. IMO
Wheels are always in the contact with the rail. Only in curved sections, one wheel has larger diameter than the other.

At no point do any of the wheels leave the rails, they just shift such that (in this gif) the left wheel slides down to a smaller size diameter and the right wheel slides up to a larger size diameter. So that, as it turns, the left wheel travels less distance while the right wheel travels larger distance per revolution (because the left rail would be shorter and the right rail would be longer in that turn). This design lets the axle rotate evenly while the two wheels travel different distances in the turn.

Its genius in its simplicity.
